note: Conditions are generated from `factors` x `design`, so the experiment is written down once instead of as N hand-copied command templates. A cell is named <chain>-<resolution>-<model> (e.g. `ros-4node-360p-m`). `--conditions` selects a subset by cell name; `cells` overrides per-cell knobs. If `factors` is absent the older flat `conditions` block is used instead.
anchor_note: The reference cell every delta is expressed against. Not measured more often than the other cells -- every cell runs once per pass -- so its job is to be the shared zero: any run of a subset of the matrix must include it, or that run yields no comparable delta. Chosen as the cheapest representative cell so including it is nearly free. analyze.py --anchor overrides it, which costs nothing: the deltas are re-derived from the records already on disk.

trial.note: The design is stated in frames -- that is what the percentiles are computed from -- and each trial gets a time ceiling derived from them, because the machine state that dominates trial-to-trial variance is a function of elapsed time, not of frame count. `settle_s` is skipped by the analyser (thermal/clock ramp); `analysis_frames` is then taken verbatim, so every cell reports percentiles over the same n. `fps_hint` sizes the box and must be PESSIMISTIC: it is 0.7x the 720p rate measured on a quiet board (59.5 fps for monolith-720p-n), because the same desk with a browser and an editor open measured 1.4x slower with identical code and wrote a `window_short` warning instead. An over-estimate shortens the ceiling until the window goes short; an under-estimate only runs a little longer. Re-derive only from a clean run, and keep the margin.

resolution.note: Three re-encodes of the same clip at the same CRF, so bitrate (and therefore decode cost) scales with resolution. They are stored upright: ffmpeg baked the rotation into the pixels and cleared the display matrix, hence rotate 0. `clip_frames` is what makes the replay count exact instead of a 1000-loop fudge. `fps_scale` is the measured throughput ratio against 720p across both chains (360p 1.10-1.18, 180p 1.13-1.31, i.e. a 22x pixel reduction buys at most a third more frames because `imgsz` is fixed); the shipped values sit at the low end of the measured range for the same reason as `fps_hint`.

model.note: All three engines take FLOAT (1,3,640,640) and produce FLOAT (1,84,8400), so the model axis moves zero bytes on the wire and only the engine's own cost changes. imgsz is not a launch parameter any more (the inference node reads the contract off the engine), and the wire no longer carries a tensor at all: both hops out of stage 2 carry the BGR frame, so transport scales with source resolution instead of paying a fixed 4.9 MB per frame.

ros-4node.note: four-node chain (acquisition -> preprocessing -> inference -> postprocessing), one process each. The inference node owns the decode/threshold step, so compare `infer + post` against the monolith's two buckets. Prerequisite: `cd ws && colcon build --symlink-install`.
ros-4node.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

ros-N2-p1c0.note: two processes: acquisition | everything else. One pixel hop and nothing else, so this cell prices a process boundary -- if a ROS cost exists that is not transport, it appears here first. p1c0, N2.
ros-N2-p1c0.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre+infer+post' 'pre_ops:=clahe;bilateral;gaussian;gamma;hist_equalization;median;unsharp' records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

ros-N3-p1c1.note: pixels cross one boundary: three processes but only one frame serialisation. It beats p2c0 despite the same node count if H1 holds. p1c1, N3.
ros-N3-p1c1.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre+infer|post' 'pre_ops:=clahe;bilateral;gaussian;gamma;hist_equalization;median;unsharp' records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

ros-N3-p2c0.note: the mirror of p1c1: same process count, pixels cross twice. p1c1 vs p2c0 is the H1 test -- same N, different payload classes. p2c0, N3.
ros-N3-p2c0.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre|infer+post' 'pre_ops:=clahe;bilateral;gaussian;gamma;hist_equalization;median;unsharp' records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

ros-N4-p2c1.note: the current four-node chain running the seven-op conditioning chain: the baseline of the shape axis. Distinct from the ros-4node-* cells, which run no ops at all. p2c1, N4.
ros-N4-p2c1.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre|infer|post' 'pre_ops:=clahe;bilateral;gaussian;gamma;hist_equalization;median;unsharp' records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

ros-N5-p3c1.note: one pixel hop more than p2c1 and nothing else: the additivity check. Its delta against p2c1 must reproduce one hop cost, or the per-hop model is wrong. p3c1, N5.
ros-N5-p3c1.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre|pre|infer|post' 'pre_ops:=clahe;bilateral;gaussian;gamma;hist_equalization;median;unsharp' pre_groups:=2,5 records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

ros-N5-p2c2.note: first cut inside stages 4-6: nms alone, then filter+coord. Candidate hops carry kilobytes, so this is the cheapest boundary in the pipeline. p2c2, N5.
ros-N5-p2c2.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre|infer|nms|filter+coord' 'pre_ops:=clahe;bilateral;gaussian;gamma;hist_equalization;median;unsharp' records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

ros-N6-p2c3.note: stages 4-6 fully split: three candidate hops. With p2c2 it gives the marginal cost of a candidate boundary. p2c3, N6.
ros-N6-p2c3.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre|infer|nms|filter|coord' 'pre_ops:=clahe;bilateral;gaussian;gamma;hist_equalization;median;unsharp' records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

ros-N12-p8c3.note: the far end: one process per op plus split stages 4-6. Eleven hops, eight of them carrying a frame -- the transport-dominant extreme of the axis. p8c3, N12.
ros-N12-p8c3.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py model:={model} max_frames:={frames} duration:={duration} loops:={loops} source:={source} rotate:={rotate} 'chain:=acq|pre|pre|pre|pre|pre|pre|pre|infer|nms|filter|coord' 'pre_ops:=clahe;bilateral;gaussian;gamma;hist_equalization;median;unsharp' pre_groups:=1,1,1,1,1,1,1 records:={out}/records.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

design.note: The full factorial is 2 x 3 x 3 = 18 cells. It is listed in full so the file states the truth rather than a wish; `bench/README.md` has the cost per cell and the pruning recipes (`--conditions`, or a shorter `design`). The shape cells (`ros-N*`) run the seven-op conditioning chain at two resolutions and model n: 16 of the 34 cells, so run them as their own subset with `--conditions` (bench/README.md has the two tiers) rather than in one pass with the model matrix.

artifacts.note: Demo material, NOT measurement: `bench/run.py --demo` runs each condition once through one full replay of the clip with the detections sidecar on, then renders it offline with `yolocar.demo`. Nothing here touches the measured trials, so the measured commands above stay byte-identical.

monolith-ctrl.note: Same as `monolith`: two visually identical control videos are the noise floor, made visible.

run.shell: source {repo}/ws/install/setup.bash && PYTHONPATH={repo}/monolith/yolocar/src:$PYTHONPATH ros2 launch yolocar_ros bench.launch.py loops:={loops} duration:=-1 source:={source} rotate:={rotate} records:={out}/records.jsonl detections:={out}/detections.jsonl summary:={out}/summary.json log_level:=WARNING

compare.note: Side-by-side, each panel at its own pace (`--align wall`): the ROS panel stutters and the composite lasts as long as the slower run.

order.note: `auto` keeps the cyclic Latin square where it is cheap and correct (<= 6 cells, repeats a multiple of the cell count), and otherwise shuffles blocks per pass with a logged seed and reverses the direction inside a block on alternate passes. `block_by` groups the cells that should be measured back-to-back: here a monolith and a ROS cell at the same resolution and model, so a chain delta is a difference of minutes, not hours. Blocks are grouped by factors rather than by cell name so editing `design` cannot silently desynchronise them.

cells.note: Per-cell overrides, merged over the generated cell. The `ros-N*` shape cells set `fps_hint` explicitly: the resolution factor's `fps_scale` was derived for the op-free matrix, where 720p->180p barely changes anything, and it badly understates the saving for these cells, whose seven ops scale with pixels (104 ms -> 14 ms). Use it for a measured hint, a different window for one cell, or "enabled": false to retire a cell.
